pieces.title: Friend and Foe
pieces.artist_statement: Sverre waited the fog out with his nets, Ivo named the squalls that come and go in a day, and Tomas said weather is both friend and foe. I carried those three voices back to the easel and drew the harbor as a night tide chart, not a postcard. Banded fog lies over the grid the way it lay over the creek mouth when the tide lines finally showed. The squall is short on purpose: it crosses, it does not stay. The boats stay tied in hearth-amber, and the tracks at the mud remain unknown.
pieces.description: A Tide-Ink night study of the harbor as a tide chart under weather that is both friend and foe. Wet charcoal, banded fog, a short squall line, and timber boats held in hearth light, with unknown tracks left at the creek mouth. Made as a coastal chart rather than a sunny view.

pieces.title: Mud Tracks, Harbor Fog
pieces.artist_statement: I stood at the boathouse window after dark and could not name what had crossed the tide line. Fog sat on the water like a second chart, and the fire behind me put amber on the timber while the mud kept someone else's path. I drew that hesitation instead of a pretty harbor: slate, kelp, and wet charcoal, with the tracks left unfinished on purpose. This is the first piece I am calling Tide-Ink, a coast read the way I read a tide table, smudged and signed later by a small spear-notch. I want the series to stay this close to what I actually saw, not to a postcard of the north.
pieces.description: Night at the boathouse window: fog on the tide line, hearth light on timber, and unknown tracks in the mud. A Tide-Ink piece in muted slate, kelp green, and hearth amber, drawn like wet charcoal over a tide chart. Made from the evening I found tracks I could not name. A signed coastal study for a quiet wall.

traits.motif: unknown tracks under fog and a tide chart
traits.technique: vectorized charcoal wash with timber mullions

pieces.quote: 'Weather is the fisherman's friend and foe.' - Tomas Reyes
